arrival.note: THE SPRING OF 1833, FROM THE COMPILER'S LIST OF THAT SEASON'S ARRIVALS. Moses and Kirkland, History of Chicago, Illinois, vol. 1 (1895), printed page 90 (claim bk_mose1_005; data/research/books/claims/moses_kirkland_history_of_chicago_v1.json): "Among the new arrivals in the spring of 1833 are the names of John Dean Caton, John K. Botsford, Silas B. Cobb, Charles Cleaver, Walter Kimball, H. W. Knickerbocker, Ezekiel Morrison, Asahel Pierce, Hibbard Porter, Stephen Rexford, Henry Whitehead, Eli B. Williams, Dr. John T. Temple, Rev. Jeremiah Porter and Rev. Allan B. Freeman." Season precision, carried at 1833-03-01, the first day this project reads a season at (hh_pearsons_hiram, hh_blodgett_tyler_k, hh_kimball_walter, minted off this same list). THE LIST SAYS "AMONG", SO IT IS A ROLL OF EXAMPLES AND NOT A REGISTER: it can date the men it names and it can never be read to exclude anybody it leaves out. THE GRADE CEILING IS THE SOURCE'S AND NOT THIS FIELD'S. Moses and Kirkland, History of Chicago, Illinois (1895) is a compiler sixty years after the fact, crediting Andreas and Hurlbut on the pages read here; every claim taken off it is transcription_mediated and none is scan_verified, so nothing drawn from it is graded above `inferred` however plainly it is printed (the rule T-1322 set for the settlers table, kept here). THE POLL'S BOUND IS NOT LOST, IT IS SUBSUMED: a man who came in the spring of 1833 was necessarily in the town for the poll of 1834. The same volume names this man again on page 348 among the eleven who organised the first Episcopal congregation in 1834 (claim bk_mose2_018), which is LATER than this field and therefore bounds nothing — it corroborates a man already here. PRIOR NOTE, KEPT: A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. poll_1834 names this person at Chicago by 31 December 1834 and nothing says when they came.

origin.note: A BIRTHPLACE, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME CLAIM. The Calumet Club roll of 1879 gives “Tolland, Conn.” as where this man was BORN; this field asks where the household came FROM, and a generation that moved west in stages frequently did not come from the state it was born in. It is carried as the best statement of origin the sources make about this household and not as a last residence.

OLD SETTLERS, 1882 — A DATE OF DEATH, AND NOTHING ABOUT 1835. John Wentworth's roll of old settlers who had died since 1 January 1881, kept for the Calumet Club and printed in the Chicago Tribune of 25 April 1882, carries “Eli B. Williams, March 24, 1881.”. That corroborates a Chicago residence before 1840 and fixes the END of this life, which this record did not carry; it is not an arrival and it places nobody in the town on 1 July 1835. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a later recollection corroborates, enriches and dates and cannot lift a rung by itself, so this record's GRADE IS UNCHANGED by it: T-0513 consolidates the identity and T-0515 regrades. Identity by rule OS1 — surname and spelled-out forename agree, one bearer (data/research/old_settlers/crosswalk.json). OLD SETTLERS, 1879 — A DATE THIS MAN GAVE FOR HIMSELF, AND STILL NOT A FACT ABOUT 1835. The Calumet Club's FIRST reception to the settlers of Chicago prior to 1840, 27 May 1879, printed its register in the proceedings (Early Chicago, Chicago, 1879, pages 84-90), and this man's entry reads “Williams, Eli B. | 1833, April, | Tolland, Conn. | 80 | Chicago.” — name, his own date of arrival, his birthplace, his age and his 1879 post-office address, in the register's five columns. The date of arrival is HIS RECOLLECTION, set down forty to sixty years after the event; the address is where he lived in 1879 and is never read as an 1835 residence. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a later recollection corroborates, enriches and dates and cannot lift a rung by itself, so this record's GRADE IS UNCHANGED by it: T-0513 consolidates the identity and T-0515 regrades. Identity by rule OS1 — surname and spelled-out forename agree, one bearer (data/research/old_settlers/crosswalk.json). FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the poll of Chicago's first city election, 2 May 1837 — “Eli B. Williams,” (f1839_v0050, printed page 41, ward 1, voting for William B. Ogden). What a match may carry, and it is short: that the man was in Chicago on 2 May 1837 and in that ward. It is written as 1837 evidence with describes_date 1837-05-02, never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on this alone. Under the ratified ladder a second contemporary source is what lifts projected_resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE, not about July 1835. The ward is a location in the CITY of 1837, whose six wards are drawn on printed page 46; it is not a location in the town of 1835 and does not place a house. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: Surname 'Williams' folds to the same string as the 1837 entry's, and the given name of both begins E. (data/research/directories/fergus_1839_election_crosswalk_1835.json and fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date — or a register four years after it — is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 1 time, as “WILLIAMS ELI B”, 1836-06-21: 1 lot in the platted town — lot 3 of block 16 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L3B16CHIOT, as printed), 0.00 acres stated in all, for $14300.00 (ls1547). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $14300.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: WILLIAMS ELI B matches Eli B Williams: the forename names Eli B Williams of the 3 people of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. THE SECOND PRESBYTERIAN ROLL — A NAME ON A CHURCH LIST THAT OPENS IN 1842, AND NEVER AN 1835 FACT. The 1892 printed membership roll of the Second Presbyterian Church of Chicago, read line by line into this repository, carries 1 line whose surname and given initial agree with this person's — “Williams, Edward M. | Profession. | April 30, 1852. | Dismissed.” (second_presb_0918, printed page 205), admitted 1852-04-30 by profession. Under the rule that decided it: Surname 'Williams' folds to the same string as the roll line's, and the given name of both begins E. WHAT THE MATCH MINTS OR REGRADES: “NOTHING. A line on a roll that opens in June 1842 cannot place a person in the town of July 1835, and this file makes no proposal that it does. What a match IS: the same surname and initial, in Chicago, within seven years — a lead for a later pass that is allowed to write people.” This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE: under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the roll is handed to the card as a thing a reader may weigh, and the verdict stays with T-0515, which applies the ladder against every source at once. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Williams, Eli B.” (poll_1834_114, line 283). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Williams' agrees with the entry's forenames; 3 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. birth_year.note: A BIRTH INTERVAL OUT OF A MAN'S OWN STATEMENT OF HIS AGE. He registered at the Calumet Club's reception to the settlers of Chicago on 27 May 1879 and gave his age as 80: "Williams, Eli B. | 1833, April, | Tolland, Conn. | 80 | Chicago.". An age of 80 completed years given on that day means the birth falls after 27 May 1798 and on or before 27 May 1799, so the birth year is 1798 or 1799. The subtraction is this project's; the page states no year of birth. IT IS A RECOLLECTION, forty-four years after the scene date — better than a recollection about somebody else, and still not a record. The merge onto this person is the old-settler crosswalk's own (OS1), in data/research/old_settlers/people.json.
